content: The Fasciculation and Elongation Protein Zeta-1 (FEZ1) is a protein in humans encoded by the FEZ1 gene. This gene is an ortholog of the Caenorhabditis elegans (C. elegans) unc-76 gene, which is essential for proper axonal bundling and elongation within axon bundles. When the human FEZ1 gene is expressed in C. elegans mutants lacking functional unc-76, it can partially restore locomotion and axonal fasciculation in these mutants. This indicates that FEZ1 plays a role in axonal outgrowth. The N-terminal region of the FEZ1 protein is highly acidic. Additionally, alternative splicing of the FEZ1 gene results in transcript variants that encode different isoforms of the protein. FEZ1 is expressed in neurons and is thought to inhibit the infection of these cells by HIV. Interactions FEZ1 has been demonstrated to interact with Protein Kinase Mζ, NBR1 (Neighbor of BRCA1 gene 1), and DISC1 (Disrupted in Schizophrenia 1).
